proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in its bearer (a LegalInstitution), is internally grounded in the structural and procedural constitution of that institution, and is realized in self-repair processes when triggered. Unlike a Role (externally grounded), a repair capacity is grounded in the institution's own internal constitution — amendment procedures, appellate structures, oversight bodies — making Disposition the correct type. It differs from LegalLegitimacyCondition and LegalExistenceCondition (existing Disposition subclasses) because it concerns ongoing functional resilience rather than existence or legitimacy conditions per se.

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess
entities.rationale: Dispositions are realized in processes. The self-repair capacity is realized in concrete self-repair processes (e.g., constitutional amendment, judicial review, legislative reform). Minting this Process class allows the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation to be properly asserted between instances of InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity and instances of InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess.

relations.rationale: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), the BFO type for internally grounded capacities.
As a specifically dependent continuant, every instance of InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity inheres in a LegalInstitution (its bearer). RO_0000052 (inheres in) is the appropriate predicate.
BFO_0000054 (realized in) links the disposition to the process in which it is manifested when conditions are met.
InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015), the class of occurrents that unfold in time.

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be further constrained to inhere only in LegalInstitution, or also in broader social institutions beyond the legal domain?

Is the intended scope purely structural/procedural (e.g., amendment procedures), or does it include informal self-corrective practices (e.g., shifting judicial interpretation)? This affects whether a single class suffices or subspecies are needed.

Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be related to the existing InstitutionalEffectiveness quality — e.g., as a disposition that, when realized, contributes to InstitutionalEffectiveness — or kept orthogonal?
Is 'capacity to repair itself' intended to cover only correction of injustice (linking to UnjustLegalSystem) or any functional repair regardless of moral valence?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'capacity of an institution to repair itself' most naturally maps to BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): a specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in the institution's own constitution (procedural rules, review mechanisms, amendment clauses) and is not merely an externally assigned role. Dispositions differ from qualities in that they need not be constantly manifested; they are triggered under appropriate conditions. The repair capacity inheres in a LegalInstitution (the bearer) and is realized in concrete InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess instances (e.g., a constitutional amendment process). Two new classes are proposed: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity as a Disposition subclass, and InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess as a Process subclass to serve as the realisation target. No existing working classes (LegalLegitimacyCondition, LegalExistenceCondition, InstitutionalEffectiveness, InstitutionalPersistence) precisely capture this concept, though relationships to InstitutionalEffectiveness and InstitutionalPersistence are worth exploring in follow-up.
